title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Analysis situs, 3rd version, 1986): a set L of 'points' and a set U of 'pieces' X, ordered by X <= Y. Each piece has a shadow ('ombre') omb(X), a subset of L, and an interior omb(X)°. Notation: x << X means x is in omb(X); x °<< X means x is in omb(X)°. For a piece X, X~ is the set of pieces below X. Earlier lemmas: Lemma 1 says that if omb(X)° meets omb(Y), then X <= Y. Lemma 2 says interiors are non-empty and that °<< is transitive in a suitable sense.

(1) Completion of Cor. 3, (iii) => (v), from p.28. Take x in omb(Z)° ∩ omb(X')°, and let X'' be any piece with Z << X'' <= X. Since Z << X'', x lies in omb(X''). So omb(X')° ∩ omb(X'') is non-empty, and Lemma 1 gives X' <= X''. Hence X' is the least element of X~^Z = {X' in X~ | Z << X'}.

(2) New corollary (numbered 3 again; really Cor. 4): X °<< Y °<< Z implies X °<< Z. This is immediate from criterion (ii), omb(Z)° ⊂ omb(X')°, since inclusion of interiors is transitive.

(3) New structure. A relation || on the points L, with axiom ML0: || is symmetric and irreflexive (x || y implies x ≠ y). Definition (1): X ⋈̸ Y ('X and Y are in good position') iff x || y for all x in omb(X) \ omb(L) and all y in omb(Y) \ omb(L). Here omb(L) is the union of omb(Z) over the common lower bounds Z <= X, Y; L plays the role of a formal 'meet' of X and Y. A sketched diamond diagram shows omb(X), omb(Y) above omb(X) ∩ omb(Y), which lies above omb(L).

By ML0, if X ⋈̸ Y then omb(X) ∩ omb(Y) = omb(L). A point in the intersection but outside omb(L) would satisfy x || x, which irreflexivity forbids. The marginal note records that ⋈̸ is symmetric and reflexive: X ⋈̸ X holds vacuously, since then omb(L) = omb(X).

(4) Lemma 3: if X, Y <= Z then X ⋈̸ Y. Faces of a common piece meet properly, i.e. their shadows meet exactly in the union of their common faces. The margin notes this will be contained in Lemma 5 (next page: ⋈̸ is inherited by smaller pieces). Indeed Z ⋈̸ Z holds trivially, and Lemma 5 then gives X ⋈̸ Y. A direct proof is begun ('Soit en effet x ∈ omb...') and continued on p.30 using ML1/ML4.

Purpose: an axiomatic, combinatorial 'tame' theory of stratified or cell-like spaces. The axioms aim to guarantee the regular-complex property that closures of two cells meet in a union of common faces.
errors: In the proof of (iii)=>(v) Grothendieck struck out 'x ∈ omb(X'')', but this step is needed. It holds because x ∈ omb(Z) ⊂ omb(X'') when Z << X''. The argument is correct once this is restored.
Numbering slip: the transitivity corollary is labelled 'Corollaire 3' although Cor. 3 is the preceding statement on p.28; it should be Cor. 4.

ideas.modern_name: minimal/carrier cell of a point or face in a regular cell complex (face poset carrier)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical combinatorial topology (regular CW complexes, Björner's face posets)

ideas.modern_name: transitivity of 'contained in the relative interior'

ideas.what: Symmetric irreflexive relation || on points and the derived 'good position' relation X ⋈̸ Y; consequence that shadows intersect exactly in the union of common lower pieces
ideas.modern_name: intersection property of regular/polyhedral cell complexes (two closed cells meet in a union of common faces); axiomatic tame topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: polyhedral complexes: classical; tame topology program: Grothendieck, Esquisse d'un programme (1984); o-minimal realisation: van den Dries et al.

ideas.modern_name: faces of a cell intersect properly

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatic 'analysis situs' gives a point set L with shadows/interiors of pieces plus a symmetric irreflexive 'separation' relation ||. From these, the regular-complex intersection property is derived as a theorem rather than assumed. This combinatorial axiomatisation of tame stratified spaces does not appear to have been developed in the literature, which went the o-minimal route instead.
missed.quote: (ML 0) la relation x || y sur L est symétrique et non réflexive ... X ⋈̸ Y ⟺ ∀ x ∈ omb(X) \ omb(L), y ∈ omb(Y) \ omb(L) ... x || y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a purely order-theoretic/combinatorial axiom system for tame topology and face posets, potentially comparable with o-minimal cell decomposition and with exit-path/stratified homotopy theory. The content of this page itself is elementary lemma work.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains routine lemma-level verifications inside an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology framework. The only mildly notable element is the introduction of the point relation || and the 'good position' relation, which belong to an unpublished program rather than a striking result.
transcription_corrections: The shadow operator is written 'omb' (ombre) on this page; the previous page's transcription 'comb' should likewise read 'omb'.
The corollary reads 'X °≪ Y °≪ Z ⟹ X °≪ Z' (double ≪ with a ring above), not a triple ⋘.
The marginal note reads roughly 'relation symétrique, réflexive' (with 'et irréflexive' struck). It refers to ⋈̸, which is reflexive vacuously, not to ||.
Bottom margin likely reads 'immédiat (je pense), sera contenu dans Lemme 5' rather than 'immédiat par zéro contenu dans lemme 5'.
The top line includes 'Soit donc' followed by a struck 'x ∈ omb(Z)° (ML2)'.
In the proof, the struck 'x ∈ omb(X'')' stands between 'x ∈ omb(X')°' and 'il vient'.
